subject: Archaeology
title: The Fertile Crescent: Where It All Began
description: A fast breakdown of The Fertile Crescent: Where It All Began for builders.

hook.text: Between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, humans built the first cities, invented writing, and created the first laws.

buildup.text: The Fertile Crescent's rich soil and reliable water made agriculture possible.

discovery.text: By 3500 BCE, Mesopotamia had cities with tens of thousands of people, temples, markets, and bureaucrats keeping records.

twist.text: Irrigation was both a gift and a curse. Salt buildup from centuries of watering eventually poisoned the soil and ruined harvests.

climax.text: Mesopotamia's innovations — writing, law, mathematics, and the wheel — spread worldwide and shaped every civilization.

punchline.text: Two rivers created a civilization. Salt in the soil eventually ended it.

quiz.question: What long-term problem threatened Mesopotamian agriculture?
options: Frequent flooding washed away all planted crops
Salt buildup from irrigation poisoned the soil over centuries
Deforestation caused the rivers to dry up completely
